mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.25%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.25% (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the federal funds rate exceeding 0.5 percentage points over one month signals abrupt monetary tightening, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5% in 1 month (p-value > 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous low federal funds rate (below 0.25%) and low inflation (CPIAUCSL below 2.0% annualized) indicate stable monetary conditions that support equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not significant: the correlation between the joint signal (FEDFUNDS<0.25% AND CPIAUCSL<2.0%) and positive 20-day returns is less than 0.05 (Rank IC < 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high unemployment regime (UNRATE > 8.0%), the market overprices economic weakness, leading to undervalued equities and subsequent positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as the market adjusts to persistent labor market weakness.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE > 8.0% (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: Strong housing market activity (HOUST above 650,000 units) reflects robust consumer demand and economic expansion, supporting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST > 650,000 (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in inflation (CPIAUCSL rising above 3.0% annualized over three months) signals potential monetary tightening, increasing real interest rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises > 3.0% annualized in 3 months (p-value > 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: In a low industrial production regime (INDPRO < 95.0), the market overreacts to economic weakness, leading to undervalued equities and subsequent positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the economy recovers.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 95.0 (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous high unemployment (UNRATE > 8.0%) and weak job growth (PAYEMS growth < 0.1% monthly) indicate deteriorating labor market conditions, signaling weak consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not significant: the correlation between the joint signal (UNRATE>8.0% AND PAYEMS growth < 0.1%) and negative 20-day returns is less than 0.05 (Rank IC < 0.05) over a 3-year rolling window.
